profile.headline: Staff Software Engineer at Ginger Labs

positions.title: Senior Staff Software Engineer
positions.description: I served as a web lead spanning multiple teams, each responsible for a business flow/process: product purchasing, purchase management, contact management, contracts, license management. Each team had 3-4 front end engineers working on distinct projects. My responsibilities included: grooming/mentoring front-end leaders on individual teams, reviewing front-end engineering designs, unblocking teams encountering difficult front-end issues, coding, working with cross-functional stakeholders (ex. UX design, Engineering, Product Management) to drive alignment, and keep teams unblocked while still meeting deadlines.

positions.title: Staff Software Engineer
positions.description: I worked on web infrastructure for a year and a half before moving to work on guiding UI efforts on LinkedIn's Enterprise Platform and Payments teams. As a lead UI engineer, my responsibilities include: leading UI engineering design, providing UI engineering technical direction for the teams, mentoring other UI engineers, working with Engineering management and cross-functional partners (Product, Design, Marketing, etc.) to coordinate project timelines and shipping of features. Oh and there's also coding and basically whatever else is needed to get stuff done.

positions.title: Web Development Manager
positions.description: For the remainder of 2014 - Q1 of 2015, I continued work on the redesign of LinkedIn’s home page and implementation of it on a new tech stack (Play framework).  I had between 4-6 direct reports, while also serving as a general engineering lead (working under a Sr. Eng Manager), managing Scrum of both web developers and server engineers.  In Q1 of 2015, I served as the overall engineering manager for the home page, as we ramped it to 100%.  This involved running Scrum, coordinating with QA, SREs, Net Ops, and upper management. I then served multiple roles on Project Voyager.  This involved managing 3 managers, setting up on-call rotations (including training the 40+ web developers on serving as an on-call engineer), and doing hands-on management of web efforts on Feed, Messaging, My Network.

positions.title: Senior/Lead Web Developer
positions.description: I continued work on Notifications, Inbox, and Mentions.  In February 2013, I became lead for the team of web developers on LI's home page, and optimized site flows (code named Skyline).  I worked with my team, providing technical guidance, and finding the right challenges for them to grow.  I worked with counterparts in Product Management, Engineering, Design, and QA to: resource and timeline projects, understand requirements, and make sure stuff gets out the door.  I also served as a lecturer for our Front-end Tech Bootcamps, helping new hires learn about our tech stacks at LinkedIn.

positions.title: Web Developer
positions.description: I was hands-on with things such as: inbox, member and guest home pages, notifications, and our email campaigns.  I worked with project managers, engineers, designers, and QA folks to keep the ball rolling and ship product.  Within the webdev team, I spent time mentoring new hires, interviewing candidates, attending conferences and presenting my learnings to our ever-growing, fun-loving team.

positions.title: Software Development Engineer
positions.description:
As a front end engineer for APT (http://apt.yahoo.com), I worked on development for the Supply Quality Management (ads classification) and Demand (campaign management) components of the APT UI.  I was also involved in constant cross-functional communication with product, UED, QA and other developers for the purposes of understanding requirements, participating in test case reviews, and doing implementation design.

Implementation involved heavy use of object-oriented JavaScript (building on top of YUI), CSS and HTML, along with using Java (Struts, JSP, and Tiles).  I also spent considerable time mentoring other front end developers, educating them with domain knowledge, and best practices in front end development.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: As a contract engineer (via CDI Corporation) for the AdSense Ads UI team, I worked on several projects regarding rendering/latency optimizations, and UI infrastructure (libraries, extensive suites of end-to-end and unit tests, build optimizations).  I was also one of the primary engineers working on the design and implementation of a new AdSense product/feature that resulted in significant revenue increases.

positions.title: E-Commerce Project Leader
positions.description: I was the primary developer responsible for the design and implementation of vertical e-commerce solutions and web-based ordering platforms.  This resulted in multiple, successful product releases, bringing about significant increases (several magnitudes) in electronic order volume.

projects.title: LinkedIn Email Strategy
projects.description:
Created a new way of thinking about our LinkedIn Email Strategy by defining a new type of email that is not marketing, but rather engagement-focused.  That strategy involved understanding the user's point in their LinkedIn journey, what elements of their network and LinkedIn activity are most important, and the actual presentation of these emails.

The link above shows how this strategy manifested in an actual email.
